title: Introduce weighted test slicer and dependency refresh planner
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds heuristic-driven test slicing to reduce premerge runtime and a planner to schedule low-risk dependency refreshes. No breaking changes to public APIs.

description:
Context: Our presubmit pipeline has grown in runtime as test surface area increases. Teams want faster feedback without losing signal from critical slow tests. At the same time, dependency refreshes (automated bump PRs) are noisy and sometimes conflict with releases.

What this PR does: Adds two cooperating features: 1) a weighted test slicer that chooses a subset of tests to run on presubmit based on historical runtime, failure impact (test importance), and recent change area; and 2) a dependency refresh planner that schedules low-risk automated dependency updates into quiet windows and batches related bumps to reduce churn. Both are feature-flagged and opt-in per-repo by default.

Design notes: The test slicer lives under tools/test-slicer and exposes a small Go library and a CLI shim used by the presubmit runner. It computes a score per test: score = importance * (1 + alpha * normalized_runtime) * recent_relevance_factor. Importance is derived from historical knock-on failures (we count tests that preceded rollbacks), runtime from historical samples, and relevance from changed file ownership maps. There is a conservative default policy that preserves >95% probability of catching high-impact failures.

The dependency refresh planner (tools/dep-refresh/planner.py) coordinates Dependabot-like bots and internal schedulers. It queries our org calendar and release windows, groups minor bumps into batches, and delays non-critical major bumps until agreed maintenance ramps. It produces a planned calendar entry per repo and can annotate generated PRs with the expected rollout window.

Testing & QA: Unit tests added for slicer heuristics and planner logic (tools/test-slicer/*_test.go, tools/dep-refresh/tests/*.py). Integration test: presubmit runner executed against a staging repo with synthetic slow and fast tests to verify that conservative defaults keep critical tests. A canary rollout was executed on three low-risk repos for 48 hours; telemetry shows median presubmit runtime reduced by ~28% with no regression in post-merge incidents.

Migration & Rollout plan: Feature-flagged behind 'ci.weighted_slicing' and 'ci.dep_planner'. Default: disabled for top-level infra and disabled for repos with <200 test runs/day. Staged opt-in: 1) internal tools repos (2/2), 2) infra-adjacent and sdk repos (2/9), 3) open opt-in for product repos after 4 weeks. Dep planner: start as advisory mode (planner suggests windows; maintainers must approve), then auto-schedule after 6 weeks.

Operational safeguards: - Telemetry events added: ci.slice_applied, ci.slice_skipped_reason, dep_planner_suggestion, dep_planner_applied. - Fallback: if test infra error rate >10% or if slice_applied causes >2x post-merge failures in a 24h rolling window, automatically disable for the repo and open a diagnostic issue. - Planner respects blackout and release windows and exposes an emergency 'pause-refresh' label.

Files changed (high level): updated CI workflow to add slicer step and to gate on flags (.github/workflows/ci.yml), new picker implementation (tools/test-slicer/*), planner python module and small CLI used by the automation bot, docs describing config knobs and rollout, a small helper in release bridge to annotate refresh PRs.

Related work: follows work in ENG-9123 (test infra stability), and complements prior presubmit decomposition efforts (presubmit-profiles). Notable difference from earlier PRs: focuses on smart sampling with conservative defaults and pairs sampling with dependency churn reduction to preserve developer velocity.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration testing in staging [x] telemetry instrumentation [x] docs updated [x] feature flags behind repo opt-in [x] reviewers approved

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI on second run.

If you want to reproduce locally: see docs/ci/weighted-test-slicing.md for example config and tools/test-slicer/README.md for CLI usage.
